_comment: The list of games DOS ex Machina can install. Fetched at run time, so
adding a game is an edit here rather than a new DXM release.
'abi' is the contract version a game's module was built against; DXM
refuses one it does not speak, and can say which side needs updating.
'module' is keyed by platform-arch, matching what DXM asks for at run
time. A missing key means that game is not available for that machine
yet - which is a thing to show the user, not an error.
'data' is separate from the module on purpose. The module is the port,
which is ours to distribute; the data is the publisher's. For freeware
we point at their own download rather than mirroring it. For anything
not freeware, kind is 'byo' and the user supplies the files.
Every artifact carries a sha256 because DXM downloads and then EXECUTES
the module. Verifying is not optional. The art carries one too, so the
on-disk cache can be keyed by it - a changed hash is a changed image,
and nothing has to guess about staleness.
'art' is shown in the navigator's right pane, for games that are merely
available as well as installed ones - so it is fetched on its own, not

games.title: SkyRoads
desc: Drive a skimmer along roads suspended over thirty alien worlds.
Fuel and oxygen run down while you line up the jumps.
